mainTopic: Washing leather and cloth on שבת, the sources for cleaning items touched by a חטאת, and items that left the courtyard
overview: The amud opens with a question about which leather needs washing (כיבוס). A משנה in מסכת שבת allows pouring water on a soft leather cushion. רבא answers that washing without rubbing (כיסכוס) does not count as washing, though for cloth, soaking alone already counts. The גמרא ties this to רבא's ruling about throwing cloth and flax seed into water on שבת, and works out that flax seed is forbidden as לישה. Then it tells how רבא publicly retracted a ruling allowing a shoe to be washed on שבת. Next the גמרא brings the פסוקים for washing the garment, breaking the clay pot and scouring the copper pot in a holy place. It also shows that the משנה's 'stringency of a חטאת' is only one example out of several. A new משנה teaches that such items that left the courtyard are brought back in, and if they became טמא they are first torn or punctured. רבינא questions tearing the garment, and the challenge from רב הונא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A soft leather cushion may have water poured on it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a question. Cushions and blankets are made of soft leather, yet a משנה allows pouring water on them on שבת, as if water on soft leather is not washing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Cushions and blankets are soft leather. Yet we learned in a משנה: if the cushion was made of leather, he may pour water on it until the dirt is gone! That suggests that pouring water on soft leather is not considered washing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that soft leather is the kind of thing that can be 'washed.' It points to a משנה that lets you pour water on a leather cushion on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If soft leather can be 'washed,' then pouring water on it should count as כיבוס and be forbidden on שבת. But the משנה allows it. So it looks like soft leather is not something that can be washed at all, and that would also matter for the law of דם חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Until it is gone (until the dirt disappears)

phrases.english: Cushions and blankets are of soft leather,
and we learned in a משנה:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in שבת 142b.

phrases.english: If it was made of leather,
he puts water on it until the dirt is gone!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion about whether soft leather needs כיבוס.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that soft leather can be washed (and so needs כיבוס).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows pouring water on soft leather on שבת. That implies that water on soft leather is not washing.

steps.title: Washing without rubbing is not washing
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that washing only counts when it includes rubbing. Pouring water without rubbing is allowed, but soft leather can still be truly washed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: any washing that has no rubbing is not called washing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. Just pouring water, without rubbing, is not considered washing at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only allowed putting water on the cushion, not scrubbing it. So soft leather can still be washed, but only through rubbing (כיסכוס). This saves the idea that soft leather can be washed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not called (it does not count as)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, for leather, washing means water together with rubbing. Water alone does not count.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Any washing that does not have rubbing
is not called washing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from the leather cushion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the term כיבוס more narrowly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Pouring water on soft leather would count as washing, so the משנה would show that soft leather cannot be washed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Washing needs rubbing. Pouring water alone is not washing, so the משנה is no problem.

steps.title: Putting water on רב's shoes
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אשי says he often splashed water on רב's leather shoes. The גמרא explains this with רבא's rule: splashing is allowed, rubbing is not. This works whether the shoes were soft leather or hard leather.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for what רב חייא בר אשי said, 'Many times I stood before רב and splashed his shoes in water': splashing, yes, but washing (with rubbing), no. If the shoes were soft leather, this fits everyone's view. If they were hard leather, it fits the view of אחרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story about רב and explains it using רבא's new rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Splashing water on shoes was allowed because there was no rubbing, so it was not washing. If the shoes were soft, everyone agrees that soft leather can be washed with rubbing. If they were hard, the warning against rubbing only makes sense according to אחרים, who hold that even hard leather can be washed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others,' the name used for a תנא whose view was quoted earlier

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא דְּאָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: And that which Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: זִימְנִין סַגִּיאִין הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב,
phrases.english: Many times I would stand before Rav,
and I would splash his shoes in water;
splashing, yes, but washing, no.
If it was soft leather, it fits everyone's view;
if it was hard leather, it fits the view of the Others.
phrases.notes: 'The Others' (אחרים) are the view quoted earlier in the סוגיא that even hard leather can be washed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דְּאָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבא's rule to explain a story about רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Splashing water on leather shoes is allowed. Rubbing them is washing and is not allowed.

steps.title: Then cloth should be allowed too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if water without rubbing is not washing, then pouring water on a cloth garment should also be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a garment too should be allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's rule. If water alone is never washing, why does the משנה forbid putting water on a cloth garment?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same משנה in שבת says that a cloth garment may only be wiped, not have water poured on it. According to רבא's rule, pouring water without rubbing should be fine for cloth as well. So the גמרא wants to know why cloth is treated more strictly.

phrases.english: If so, a garment too!
phrases.notes: The same משנה says a cloth garment may only be wiped, not have water poured on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רבא's rule from the step before.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that washing without rubbing is not washing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that is true, pouring water on cloth should be allowed. But the משנה forbids it.

steps.title: For cloth, soaking is washing
steps.stepSummary: Cloth is different. Simply soaking it in water already counts as washing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A garment: its soaking is its washing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that cloth works differently from leather. Getting cloth wet already counts as washing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leather needs rubbing to count as washed. Cloth absorbs water, so soaking it is already washing. That is why the משנה forbids pouring water on cloth but allows it on leather.
steps.whatToRemember: Leather counts as washed only with rubbing. Cloth counts as washed just by soaking it.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא's rule about needing rubbing applies to leather, not to cloth.

phrases.english: A garment: its soaking is its washing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about cloth.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cloth and leather follow the same rule about rubbing.
steps.terutzMaskana: For cloth, soaking alone is washing. Only leather needs rubbing.

steps.title: רבא's ruling about a cloth and flax thrown into water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבא is consistent. He also ruled that throwing a cloth into water on שבת makes a person liable, and so does throwing flax into water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא follows his own reasoning, for רבא said: if someone threw a cloth into water, he is liable. If he threw flax into water, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the idea 'soaking cloth is washing' matches another ruling of רבא. This also sets up the next question about the flax.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Throwing a cloth into water is liable even with no rubbing, because soaking cloth is washing. That matches the answer just given. רבא also gave a second case, flax, and the גמרא will examine it next.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning (consistent with his other view)

phrases.english: Rava follows his own reasoning,
for Rava said:
If he threw a cloth into water, he is liable.
If he threw flax into water, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the rule 'soaking cloth is washing' to another ruling of רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Throwing a cloth into water on שבת is liable as washing. Throwing flax into water is also liable.

steps.title: Why is throwing flax seed into water forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The cloth case is clear, because it is washing. But what is the reason a person is liable for throwing flax seed into water?
steps.simpleTranslation: The cloth makes sense, because he is washing. But flax seed, what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the cloth case and asks about the flax case. Flax seed is not clothing, so why would soaking it break שבת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Washing only applies to cloth, so it cannot explain liability for flax seed. The גמרא wants to know which מלאכה is involved. Steps 8-11 work out the answer.

phrases.english: It makes sense for a cloth: he is doing washing;
but flax seed, what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא סוּדָר – עָבֵיד כִּיבּוּס; אֶלָּא זֶרַע פִּשְׁתָּן מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the second case in רבא's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which מלאכה makes a person liable for throwing flax seed into water on שבת.

steps.title: Is flax forbidden because it sprouts?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that flax is forbidden because it sprouts in water, and then rejects this: wheat and barley also sprout, and nobody forbids them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it is because it sprouts — if so, wheat and barley should also be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out a possible reason for the flax rule and immediately knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If sprouting, which is like planting, were the problem, then putting wheat or barley in water would also be forbidden. Since it is not, sprouting cannot be the reason for flax.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say — introduces a suggested answer

phrases.english: And if you would say it is because it sprouts
phrases.notes: The idea is that sprouting in water would be like planting, which is forbidden on שבת.

phrases.english: If so, wheat and barley too should be forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to Step 7's question and rejects it at once.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that flax is forbidden because it sprouts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wheat and barley also sprout in water, yet soaking them is not forbidden.

steps.title: Flax gives off slimy liquid
steps.stepSummary: The real reason is that flax seeds give off a slimy liquid when soaked, unlike wheat and barley.
steps.simpleTranslation: These flax seeds have slimy discharges.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reason for the flax rule that separates flax from wheat and barley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not sprouting. Flax seeds release a sticky slime in water, and wheat and barley do not.

phrases.english: These have slimy discharges.
phrases.notes: "These" means the flax seeds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8 by pointing to something only flax has.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Flax is forbidden because it sprouts, like planting.
steps.terutzMaskana: Flax is different because it gives off slime when soaked.

steps.title: Hides also give off slime
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: animal hides also give off slime in water, so they should be forbidden too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, hides should also be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the slime reason with another case that seems the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soaked hides also release liquid. If slime alone were the problem, soaking hides would also be forbidden, but it is not.

phrases.english: If so, hides too should be forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The slime reason for the flax rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Hides also give off liquid in water, yet soaking them is allowed.

steps.title: Flax seeds stick together, which is kneading
steps.stepSummary: With flax, the slime makes the seeds clump together, and that counts as kneading. Hides do not clump.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, he is doing kneading.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final reason for the flax rule: it counts as the forbidden act of kneading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slime matters only because it glues the seeds into one mass, just like kneading dough. Hides do not join together, so no kneading happens.

keyTerms.meaning: Kneading, one of the forbidden מלאכות of שבת

steps.whatToRemember: Throwing flax seed into water on שבת is forbidden because the seeds stick together, which counts as לישה. It is not because of planting or slime alone.

phrases.english: There, he is doing kneading.
phrases.notes: "There" means the flax: its slime glues the seeds together into one mass.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10 and closes the question of Step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any soaking that gives off slime is forbidden, so hides should be too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Flax is forbidden as לישה because the seeds clump together. Hides do not.

steps.title: רבא rules that washing a shoe on שבת is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches in public that a person may wash a shoe on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: It is permitted to wash a shoe on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story of רבא giving a public ruling. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This seems to go against the rule from Step 3, that splashing is allowed but real washing is not. The next step brings that challenge.

phrases.english: Rava taught in public:
It is permitted to wash a shoe on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story connected to the shoe topic of Step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא publicly allowed washing a shoe on שבת.

steps.title: רב פפא challenges רבא from רב's shoes
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא points out that רב חייא בר אשי only splashed water on רב's shoes, which shows that splashing is allowed but washing is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: But רב חייא בר אשי said: Many times I stood before רב and splashed water on his shoes. Splashing, yes, but washing, no!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges רבא's ruling using the report about רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The report says only splashing was done. That suggests the line is drawn there: splashing is allowed and full washing is forbidden. This goes against רבא's public ruling.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi say:

phrases.aramaic: זִימְנִין סַגִּיאִין הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב,
phrases.english: Many times I would stand before Rav,
and splash his shoes with water;
Splashing, yes, but washing, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's ruling in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that washing a shoe on שבת is allowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב only allowed splashing, which shows that real washing is forbidden.

steps.title: רבא publicly admits his mistake
steps.stepSummary: רבא appoints a speaker and announces in public that he was wrong: splashing is allowed, washing is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא went back, set up a speaker for himself, and taught: The things I told you were my mistake. Truly, this is what they said: splashing is allowed, washing is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא accepts the challenge and openly corrects his earlier ruling before the public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The final rule matches Step 3: water without rubbing is fine on שבת, and real washing is not. רבא's ruling in Step 12 is withdrawn completely.

keyTerms.meaning: He set up a speaker who repeats the teacher's words loudly to the crowd

steps.whatToRemember: Final rule for shoes on שבת: שכשוך (splashing) is allowed, כיבוס (washing with rubbing) is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא teaches us that a great רב admits a mistake in public, in the same way he made the mistake.

phrases.aramaic: הֲדַר אוֹקֵי רָבָא אָמוֹרָא עֲלֵיהּ וּדְרַשׁ:
phrases.english: Rava went back, set up a speaker for himself, and taught:
phrases.notes: The speaker is the person who repeats the lesson loudly to the crowd, so everyone would hear the correction.

phrases.english: The things that I said before you
are my mistake;
but truly, this is what they said:
Splashing is permitted, washing is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבָרִים שֶׁאָמַרְתִּי לִפְנֵיכֶם טָעוּת הֵם בְּיָדִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא accepts רב פפא's challenge from Step 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Splashing water on shoes is allowed on שבת; washing them is forbidden.

steps.title: Where do we learn the משנה's rule of washing in a holy place?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, which says the washing and cleaning must be done in a holy place, and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The washing in a holy place, etc. From where are these things learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the words of the משנה and asks for the פסוק behind them. This sets up the answers in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists three things: washing the garment, breaking the clay pot, and scouring the copper pot, all in a holy place. The גמרא wants a source for each.

keyTerms.meaning: A holy place, inside the עזרה
From where are these things learned?
Etc. — the rest of the quote

phrases.english: The washing is in a holy place, etc.
From where are these things learned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שבת discussion and returns to the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוקים for washing, breaking and scouring in a holy place.

steps.title: Source for washing the garment in a holy place
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings the פסוק: "You shall wash in a holy place."
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: "You shall wash in a holy place."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first part of the question with a פסוק that says it outright.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about a garment splashed with the blood of a חטאת says it must be washed in a holy place. That is a direct source for the משנה.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
"You shall wash in a holy place."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first part of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק explicitly says to wash in a holy place.

steps.title: Source for breaking the clay pot
steps.stepSummary: The next פסוק says a clay pot in which the חטאת was cooked must be broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we learn breaking a clay pot? The פסוק says: "And the clay vessel in which it is cooked shall be broken."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks and answers the second part: the source for breaking the clay pot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The breaking comes from the very next פסוק. Since it continues the same passage, it shares the requirement of a holy place.

phrases.english: The breaking of a clay vessel, from where?
The verse teaches:
"And the clay vessel in which it is cooked shall be broken."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:21

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of sources begun in Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 6:21 requires the clay pot to be broken.

steps.title: Source for scouring and rinsing the copper pot
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק continues: a copper pot used for the חטאת must be scoured and rinsed in water.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we learn scouring and rinsing a copper vessel? The פסוק says: "And if it was cooked in a copper vessel, it shall be scoured and rinsed in water."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list with the source for cleaning the copper pot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A copper pot is not broken like a clay pot; it is cleaned. This also comes from the same passage of פסוקים.
steps.whatToRemember: All three cleaning rules of the משנה come from ויקרא 6:20-21: wash the garment, break the clay pot, scour and rinse the copper pot.

phrases.english: Scouring and rinsing a copper vessel, from where?
The verse teaches:
"And if it was cooked in a copper vessel,
it shall be scoured and rinsed in water."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:21

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of sources from Steps 16-17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 6:21 requires the copper pot to be scoured and rinsed.

steps.title: Are there no other stringencies of a חטאת?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says "this is a stringency of a חטאת." The גמרא asks why it leaves out another one: its blood is brought into the inner sanctuary.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a stringency of a חטאת, etc. And there are no more? But there is the fact that its blood enters the inner sanctuary!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה and challenges its list as incomplete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some חטאות have their blood sprinkled inside the היכל, which is a big extra stringency. So why does the משנה act as if the cleaning rules are the only stringencies?

keyTerms.meaning: The innermost part, inside the היכל

phrases.english: This is a stringency of a sin offering, etc.
And there are no more?!
But there is the fact that its blood enters the innermost place!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's list of stringencies of a חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The list leaves out the stringency that its blood is brought inside.

steps.title: The משנה speaks about outer חטאות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is only talking about חטאות whose blood is placed on the outer מזבח, so the inner rule does not apply to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: With the outer sin offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is limited to one type of חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only inner חטאות have their blood brought inside. The משנה is discussing outer חטאות, so it is right not to mention that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Outer sin offerings, whose blood goes on the outer מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Outer and inner חטאות are both truly חטאות. The difference is only where the blood goes, so the inner rule simply does not apply to the outer ones.

phrases.english: It is speaking of the outer sin offerings.
phrases.notes: These are חטאות whose blood goes on the outer מזבח, not inside the היכל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19 by narrowing what the משנה is talking about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה covers all חטאות, so its list is missing a rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה covers only outer חטאות, where blood is not brought inside.

steps.title: What about blood that enters inside?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה leaves out another stringency: if the blood of an outer חטאת is brought inside the היכל, the קרבן becomes פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is another stringency: if its blood is brought inside, it becomes disqualified!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another possible stringency of a חטאת that the משנה did not mention. If an outer חטאת's blood is carried inside the היכל, the חטאת becomes פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 limited the משנה to outer חטאות, so the rule that 'its blood goes inside' was taken off the list. Now the גמרא finds a rule that does fit outer חטאות: if their blood wrongly goes inside, they are ruined. So why doesn't the משנה list this rule as a stringency too?

keyTerms.meaning: Inside, meaning into the היכל (the Sanctuary)
Disqualified; the קרבן can no longer be used

phrases.english: That if its blood entered
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves out the opening words: 'But there is the stringency...'

phrases.english: inside, it is disqualified!
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some don't. Just read it as 'inside.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new missing stringency that fits even outer חטאות, after step 20 dismissed the first one
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that washing the blood is 'the' stringency of a חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Outer חטאות have another stringency: they become פסול if their blood enters inside. The משנה should have listed it.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who holds that the blood of any קרבן becomes פסול if it enters the היכל to atone. So this rule is not special to a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רבי עקיבא, who says: any blood that entered the היכל to atone becomes disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this rule is not unique to a חטאת. According to רבי עקיבא, every קרבן's blood is disqualified if it is brought into the היכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists only stringencies that a חטאת has and other קרבנות do not. רבי עקיבא applies the 'blood went inside' rule to all קרבנות. So this rule does not set a חטאת apart, and the משנה had no reason to list it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary building inside the Temple
To atone; here, to bring blood inside as if for atonement

phrases.english: It is like Rabbi Akiva, who says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל דָּמִים שֶׁנִּכְנְסוּ לַהֵיכָל לְכַפֵּר – פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.english: Any blood that entered the Sanctuary to atone is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a חטאת is disqualified when its blood goes inside, so the משנה should list this rule
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי עקיבא, all קרבנות are disqualified this way, so the rule is not a special stringency of a חטאת

steps.title: What about atoning for sins with כרת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about another stringency: a חטאת atones for sins that carry כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is another stringency: it atones for those who are liable to כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third possible stringency the משנה left out. A חטאת atones for sins whose deliberate version is punished with כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenger treats atoning for sins that carry כרת as a feature that sets a חטאת apart. If so, it looks like another stringency of a חטאת. So why isn't it in the משנה?

keyTerms.meaning: People liable to כרת (being cut off), the heavenly punishment for very serious sins

phrases.english: For they atone for those liable to karet!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge in the same pattern as step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's list of what is special about a חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Atoning for כרת sins is a unique feature of a חטאת, yet the משנה does not mention it.

steps.title: Not every חטאת atones for כרת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's rule also covers the חטאת brought for שמיעת הקול, which does not atone for a כרת sin. So the כרת feature does not apply to every חטאת in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה also covers the חטאת brought for 'hearing the voice.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה also includes a חטאת that has nothing to do with כרת: the one brought for שמיעת הקול. So 'atoning for כרת' does not apply to every חטאת the משנה covers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה wants a stringency that is true of every חטאת it talks about. The חטאת of שמיעת הקול is brought for a false oath about testimony, and that sin has no כרת. So the כרת feature cannot be listed as a rule for all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'hearing the voice'; falsely swearing that you have no testimony to give

phrases.english: With a sin offering of hearing the voice.
phrases.notes: From ויקרא 5:1: someone who hears a call to testify and falsely swears he knows nothing. This sin has no כרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the rule does not apply to every case the משנה covers
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every חטאת atones for a כרת sin, so this should be listed
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה also includes the חטאת of שמיעת הקול, which has no כרת, so the feature is not universal

steps.title: What about the four placements?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about another stringency: a חטאת needs four placements of blood on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is another stringency: it requires four placements!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a fourth possible stringency. A חטאת's blood must be placed four times on the מזבח, while other קרבנות need fewer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four placements looks like a clear feature that belongs only to a חטאת. Once again the גמרא asks why the משנה left it out.

keyTerms.meaning: Four placements of blood on the מזבח

phrases.english: For it requires four placements!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another challenge in the same chain
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's list of what is special about a חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Needing four placements is unique to a חטאת and should have been listed.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי ישמעאל, who holds that the blood of all קרבנות needs four placements on the four corners. So this rule is not special to a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רבי ישמעאל, who says: all blood needs four placements on four corners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the same way it did with רבי עקיבא. According to רבי ישמעאל, every קרבן needs four placements, so this does not set a חטאת apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same type of answer as step 22. The rule is shared by all קרבנות according to one תנא, so it is not a unique stringency of a חטאת.

phrases.english: It is like Rabbi Yishmael, who says:
All blood requires four placements
on the four corners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a חטאת needs four placements
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי ישמעאל, all קרבנות need four placements, so this is not unique to a חטאת

steps.title: There are even more unique rules
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the whole line of questioning. A חטאת also has other unique rules: the blood goes on the קרן, it is placed with a finger, and it goes on the edge of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, isn't there the corner? Isn't there the finger? Isn't there the edge?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps back and questions the starting assumption of steps 19-26. Even after all these answers, a חטאת still has other unique rules that the משנה does not mention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenges all assumed the משנה was listing every stringency of a חטאת. But the קרן, the finger, and the edge are clearly unique to a חטאת, and no answer removes them. So that assumption must be wrong. This step sets up the conclusion that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning; a way of turning an argument back on the one asking

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not answer the earlier questions. It shows that they rest on a wrong assumption: that the משנה meant to list every stringency.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, isn't there the corner!
phrases.notes: The חטאת's blood goes on the raised corner at the top of the מזבח, not on its lower wall.

phrases.english: Isn't there the finger! Isn't there its edge!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the premise behind the whole chain of challenges in steps 19-26
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole series of questions asking why the משנה left out other stringencies
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The questions assumed the משנה gives a complete list, yet other unique rules of a חטאת are clearly missing

steps.title: The משנה picked one of several stringencies
steps.stepSummary: The conclusion: the משנה just mentioned one stringency out of two or three. It never meant to give a full list.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it mentioned one out of two or three stringencies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the משנה chose one example of a חטאת's strictness, without listing all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because a חטאת has several unique rules, leaving some of them out is not a problem. The phrase 'this is a stringency of a חטאת' means 'here is one stringency,' not 'here is the only one.'
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's 'this is a stringency of a חטאת' gives one example, not a complete list. All the questions about missing stringencies fall away.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא חַד מִתְּרֵי תְּלָתָא חוּמְרֵי נָקֵט.
phrases.english: Rather, it mentioned one of two or three stringencies.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא חַד מִתְּרֵי תְּלָתָא חוּמְרֵי נָקֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the pushback in step 27
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה mentions one stringency of a חטאת as an example and does not claim it is the only one.

steps.title: משנה: garments and clay pots that left the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: A garment splashed with חטאת blood that left the courtyard is brought back in and washed in a holy place. If it became טמא, it is torn first. A clay pot that left is brought back in and broken in a holy place. If it became טמא, it is punctured first.
steps.simpleTranslation: A garment that went outside the curtains is brought back in and washed in a holy place. If it became impure outside, you tear it, bring it in, and wash it in a holy place. A clay pot that went outside is brought back in and broken in a holy place. If it became impure outside, you make a hole in it, bring it in, and break it in a holy place.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that the cleaning of a חטאת garment or pot must happen inside the courtyard, even if the item went out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Washing and breaking must be done in a holy place, so an item that went out has to come back in. But you may not bring something טמא into the עזרה. So the item is first damaged until it can no longer hold טומאה (torn or punctured), and then it is brought in.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside the curtains, meaning outside the Temple courtyard
He makes a hole in it, which makes it stop being a vessel that can be טמא
A holy place, meaning inside the courtyard

steps.confusionAlert: Tearing or puncturing is NOT the required cleaning. It is a first step that makes the item טהור so it may enter the courtyard. The real cleaning (washing or breaking) still happens inside.

phrases.english: MISHNA
A garment that went outside the curtains
phrases.notes: This is a garment that had חטאת blood splashed on it and still needs washing (ויקרא 6:20).

phrases.english: is brought back in, and one washes it in a holy place.
If it became impure outside the curtains,
he tears it, brings it in, and washes it in a holy place.
phrases.notes: Tearing makes the garment stop counting as something that can be טמא, so it may now enter.

phrases.english: A clay pot that went outside the curtains
is brought back in, and one breaks it in a holy place.
If it became impure outside the curtains,
he makes a hole in it, brings it in, and breaks it in a holy place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It moves from the earlier discussion of the חטאת's special rules to the handling of garments and pots that the חטאת touched.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Washing a garment and breaking a clay pot must be done inside the courtyard. If the item became טמא outside, it is first torn or punctured so it becomes טהור, and then it is brought in.

steps.title: משנה: copper pots that left the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: A copper pot that left the courtyard is brought back in, then scoured and rinsed in a holy place. If it became טמא, it is first broken open with a large hole, then brought in, scoured, and rinsed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A copper pot that went outside the curtains is brought back in and scoured and rinsed in a holy place. If it became impure outside, you break a hole in it, bring it in, and scour and rinse it in a holy place.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list with copper pots, which follow the same pattern as the other items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A metal pot is not broken. It is scoured and rinsed. If it became טמא, a large hole is made so it stops being a usable vessel and becomes טהור, and only then is it brought into the courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: He breaks a large hole in it, so it stops being a vessel

steps.whatToRemember: Same pattern for all three items: if it went out, bring it back and clean it inside. If it became טמא, first damage it so it is טהור, then bring it in.

phrases.english: A copper pot that went outside the curtains
is brought back in, and one scours it and rinses it in a holy place.
If it became impure outside the curtains,

phrases.aramaic: פּוֹחֲתוֹ, וְנִכְנָס וּמוֹרְקוֹ וְשׁוֹטְפוֹ בְּמָקוֹם קָדוֹשׁ.
phrases.english: he breaks a hole in it, brings it in, and scours and rinses it in a holy place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It continues the same משנה with the third item, a copper pot.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A copper pot is scoured and rinsed inside the courtyard. If it became טמא, a hole is broken in it first.

steps.title: רבינא: a torn garment is no longer a garment
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges the משנה's rule to tear an impure garment. The תורה says to wash a 'garment', and once it is torn it is not a garment anymore.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא objects: 'He tears it'? The תורה said 'a garment' must be washed, and a torn one is not a garment!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with רבינא attacking the משנה's instruction to tear an impure garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The washing rule in the תורה applies to a 'בגד'. If tearing turns it into rags so it is no longer a garment, then the washing requirement should fall away. So why would the משנה say to wash it after tearing?

keyTerms.meaning: Objects to it, raises a challenge
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

phrases.english: GEMARA
Ravina objects to this: He tears it?!
The Torah said "a garment,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:20

phrases.english: and this is not a garment!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It challenges the tearing rule in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that an impure garment is torn and then washed in a holy place.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The washing rule depends on the item being a 'בגד'. Tearing it means it is no longer a בגד, so there should be nothing left to wash.

steps.title: He leaves a small cloth's worth untorn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that he does not tear the whole garment. He leaves a piece the size of a מעפורת (a small cloth) intact, so it still counts as a garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where he leaves in it enough for a small cloth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבינא: the tearing is partial, and a piece big enough to count as a garment is left whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a מעפורת-sized piece stays intact, the item still counts as a 'בגד', so the washing rule still applies. The answer assumes the tearing is still enough to make it טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: Enough for a מעפורת, a small cloth or wrap

phrases.english: It is where he leaves in it enough for a small cloth.
phrases.notes: He means: tear most of it, but keep a small-cloth-sized piece whole, so it is still a garment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers רבינא's challenge in step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the tearing is partial.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Tearing destroys the garment completely, so the תורה's word 'בגד' no longer fits.
steps.terutzMaskana: A מעפורת-sized piece is left intact, so it is still a garment that must be washed.

steps.title: רב הונא: leaving a small cloth keeps it impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the answer using רב הונא. A torn garment only becomes טהור if no מעפורת-sized piece is left. If one is left, the pieces stay connected and the garment stays טמא, so it still cannot be brought in.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב הונא said: They only taught this when he did not leave enough for a small cloth. But if he left enough for a small cloth, it counts as connected!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 32 by quoting רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of tearing was to make the garment טהור so it could enter the courtyard. רב הונא says that leaving a מעפורת-sized piece keeps the garment one connected item, so it is still טמא. That means the answer fixes רבינא's problem but breaks the reason for tearing in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? It opens a challenge
They only taught this when..., which limits a rule
A connection: the pieces count as one item, so the טומאה stays

steps.confusionAlert: There is a squeeze here. Leave too little, and it is not a 'garment' (רבינא's point). Leave a מעפורת, and it is still טמא (רב הונא's point). The גמרא takes up this problem on the next amud.

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Rav Huna say:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא שִׁיֵּיר בָּהּ כְּדֵי מַעְפּוֹרֶת,
phrases.english: They taught this only when he did not leave in it enough for a small cloth,
phrases.notes: 'This' means the rule that tearing a garment makes it טהור.

phrases.english: but if he left in it enough for a small cloth,
it counts as connected!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It challenges the answer given in step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that a מעפורת-sized piece is left untorn.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רב הונא, leaving a מעפורת keeps the garment connected and still טמא. Then the tearing does not make it טהור, so it still may not be brought into the courtyard.
